title: Files on Windows vfs lost when file names contain CJK punctuations

#### What is the problem you are having with rclone?

As an Asian user, it's very common that we use CJK punctuations in file names.
And since rclone has a Windows restricted characters replacement mechanism by default, it bugs our Asian users a lot.
If you use both Windows and Linux devices, the file name is inconsistent between two platforms.
So I try to achieve consistent file names by disabling this mechanism completely using `--local-encoding None` `--s3-encoding None`
But it seams that vfs on Windows doesn't honour `--local-encoding` arguments and drop files

Reproduce steps:
1. Mount a volume on Windows with `--local-encoding None` and `--s3-encoding None`
2. Copy some files that name contain CJK punctuations which are replacements of Windows restricted characters
    eg: `foo：bar.txt`
3. Unmount volume and remount volume
4. Uploaded files lost

#### What is your rclone version (output from `rclone version`)

v1.66.0

#### Which OS you are using and how many bits (e.g. Windows 7, 64 bit)

Windows 11, 64bit

#### Which cloud storage system are you using? (e.g. Google Drive)

S3 Compliant Storage (Cloudflare R2)

#### The command you were trying to run (e.g. `rclone copy /tmp remote:tmp`)

```
%ProgramData%\Programs\rclone\rclone.exe ^
    -vv ^
    --use-mmap ^
    --local-encoding None ^
    --s3-encoding None ^
    --s3-directory-markers ^
    --use-server-modtime ^
    --update ^
  mount Private: * ^
    --network-mode ^
    --vfs-cache-mode=writes ^
    --vfs-fast-fingerprint ^
    --vfs-read-chunk-size 5M ^
    --vfs-read-chunk-size-limit 80M ^
    --vfs-disk-space-total-size 1T ^
    --vfs-cache-max-age 1m ^
    --vfs-used-is-size ^
    --volname myCloud
```

#### A log from the command with the `-vv` flag (e.g. output from `rclone -vv copy /tmp remote:tmp`)
